pills.text: THE STATE-THEORY PROBLEM AND ITS STAKES
CENTRAL FOCUS
[1] STATE THEORY ASKS ABOUT ORIGIN, PURPOSE, LIBERTY, INEQUALITY
[2] GAUBA COMPARES COMPETING IMAGES RATHER THAN ANNOUNCING ONE
[3] THE STATE APPEARS AS ETHICAL WHOLE, INSTRUMENT, CLASS
[4] A THEORY BECOMES MISLEADING WHEN ITS PARTIAL INSIGHT
STATE THEORY IS PLURAL BECAUSE POLITICAL POWER HAS SEVERAL
ANSWER USE

sequence: CENTRAL FOCUS
The State-Theory Problem and Its Stakes
[1] State theory asks about origin, purpose, liberty, inequality, society and change.
[2] Gauba compares competing images rather than announcing one final state doctrine.
[3] The state appears as ethical whole, instrument, class relation and group coordinator.

pills.text: DEFINITIONS AND THE CHAPTER SEQUENCE

[1] ORGANIC THEORY TREATS THE STATE AS NATURAL; CONTRACT

[4] GANDHIAN, FEMINIST AND PLURALIST VIEWS CHALLENGE COERCION, PATRIARCHY

Definitions and the Chapter Sequence
[1] Organic theory treats the state as natural; contract theory treats it as artificial.
[2] Laissez-faire limits the state, while welfare liberalism makes freedom enabling.
[3] Marxist, communitarian and post-colonial views relocate the source of political power.

stages.title: CRITICAL, COMMUNITARIAN, GANDHIAN, FEMINIST AND PLURALIST THINKERS

ANSWER USE

[3] Communitarians stress embedded selves; post-colonial theory stresses inherited state forms.
